interest: Weighs repatriating vs. retaining Japanese technicians in postwar China.
overview: March 1946 memo: Magill proposes U.S.-financed technical experts and labor training to speed China's repatriation of retained Japanese personnel.

people.name: Robert N. Magill
people.role: Division of Economic Development (ED), Department of State

people.name: Donald P. MacDonald
people.role: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs (JK), Department of State

people.name: Philip H. Trezise
people.role: Lieutenant, Office of Research and Intelligence (ORI), Department of State

people.name: George C. Marshall
people.role: General / Special Presidential Envoy to China

people.name: James K. Penfield
people.role: Office of Far Eastern Affairs (FE), Department of State

subfiles.about: Discussion among State Department economic and intelligence officers concerning U.S. measures to encourage China to repatriate Japanese industrial, technical, and managerial personnel.
subfiles.summary: Magill's March 1946 memo of conversation with MacDonald and Trezise proposes financing American technical experts and Chinese labor training, possibly tied to an Export-Import Bank credit or Marshall's Chongqing mission, to speed China's repatriation of retained Japanese industrial personnel; ED would plan the policy's economics.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Repatriation of Japanese Industrial Labor from China and Manchuria
